tagline: Out the North Fork to the ferry at Orient Point.
intro: Route 25 runs east out of Southold along the North Fork, through Greenport and the hamlet of Orient, to the end of the road at the Orient Point ferry landing. On the way it passes wineries, broad farms and wild wetlands, with the water showing now and then, and it finishes on an open view of the Atlantic.
FHWA calls it a wine-and-water byway. Out past the point, five minutes by boat across Plum Gut, lies Plum Island and its Department of Agriculture lab, where many Orient people make their living.

moments.title: Southold
moments.text: Puritans from New Haven Colony settled here in October 1640, in what most histories call the first English settlement on Long Island in the future New York.

moments.title: Greenport
moments.text: A whaling and shipbuilding village whose people knew the waters well enough during Prohibition to outrun the Coast Guard.

moments.title: Orient
moments.text: The easternmost hamlet on the fork has houses from three centuries, and locals joke that a new one is anything built since World War II.
